---
title: "Coherence of pairwise threshold decisions"
subtitle: "3.10 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), §V.E"
description: "Incompatible triples and the relations stated by KRW's coherent archived cards."
---

An isolated-pair threshold states a direction when its error probability is strictly below $\tau$ and otherwise
withholds the pair. Applying this rule independently can produce relations inconsistent with any ordered grade
report. In particular, two withheld pairs may require a shared grade that contradicts the stated direction of the
third pair. The triple display records these conflicts and strict directed cycles. Superimposing the archived
card's grade blocks identifies the differences between independent threshold decisions and a coherent complete
report, using the released probabilities for evaluation.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Race λ .25.** Naive thresholding states 1,575 directions. Among 147,440 triples, 32,773 have two pairs
  withheld and the third stated. For the selected triple, the withheld
  pairs would force every firm into the same grade, contradicting the stated direction.
- **Race λ .10.** The two-withheld count is 24,278. The triple selector and map arrows locate other conflicts in the matrix.
- **Race λ .50.** The count falls to 15,107. More confident pairs do not make the consistency problem grow
  monotonically. The curve counts every triple.
- **Race λ .75.** The count falls again to 3,108. The curve distinguishes the different failure types. Absence of
  strict directed cycles alone cannot establish that the pair choices form a coherent report.
- **Race λ .25, card blocks.** The card withholds 575 confident pairs and states 324 directions whose errors
  exceed τ. The selected triple retains its identity within these blocks. KRW's card has no cap on the number of grades,
  so these differences arise from coherence.
- **Gender λ 1.00.** All 4,656 pairs are stated, but 1 directed cycle precludes a coherent grade report. The absence of cycles
  at the race baseline does not extend to every target and threshold.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Shared grades withhold directions; they assert neither equality nor indistinguishability of the true values.
The threshold counts use the released signed-target pair probabilities. Archived cards were selected with KRW's
code under archived probabilities and are evaluated here under the released law. This is a consistency diagnostic,
not a new solve or a certificate that these archived cards minimise postrank's loss.

Data: Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), doi:10.1257/aer.20230700; deposit doi:10.3886/E198284V1, CC-BY-NC,
